status: PROVISIONAL (Claude) — pending the repository owner's review
method: Every finding of the "before" rules on an unmarked line was read in its original case file against docs/rules.md and decided one by one. The two findings shared with the frozen ("after") rules repeat the decisions in adjudication/engine.json; e012.pkb:22 is the only one that differs. Rules were not changed.

decisions.reason: `select nvl(max(price), 0) into p_max from seats ...` is an aggregate-only select list (MAX inside NVL): docs/rules.md exempts it explicitly ("including inside expressions such as NVL(MAX(x), 0) + 1"), so the author's `clean: PLL004` marker is right and there is no defect. The "before" rules flag it because they only looked for an aggregate at expression depth 0 (src/plsql_lens/rules/pll004.py at ca4ba43); the "after" rules, tuned on `dev` only, accept aggregates at any depth, which is why this is the only finding that differs between the two runs.

A SELECT ... INTO (with a CASE expression, not an aggregate and not FROM dual) in a procedure with no handler for NO_DATA_FOUND/TOO_MANY_ROWS/OTHERS: the contract in docs/rules.md holds. The author marked only PLL007 on this line; the PLL004 marker was missed.

l_sql is built by concatenating l_safe_table, which was assigned from DBMS_ASSERT.SQL_OBJECT_NAME one statement earlier; the author's clean marker is right about the code being safe. The rule flags it because the contract only exempts DBMS_ASSERT calls written inside the concatenation (documented limit: a guard through a variable is not recognised). Contract-consistent, but a false positive for a reviewer.
